label: Regulatory Programme Risk Taxonomy & Register
description: Build a structured risk taxonomy and RAID register for a large regulatory-change programme — interpretation, supervisory-deadline, dependency/sequencing, resourcing, scope-creep, and evidence/audit-trail risk — with programme-governance and escalation structures.

claudeKnowledge.description: EU financial-services regulatory calendars and application dates (AMLR (EU) 2024/1624, AMLA Reg (EU) 2024/1620, AMLD6 (EU) 2024/1640, DORA (EU) 2022/2554, NIS2 (EU) 2022/2555, MiCA (EU) 2023/1114, TFR (EU) 2023/1113, EU AI Act (EU) 2024/1689, CSRD (EU) 2022/2464 + ESRS); programme/portfolio risk frameworks (MoP, MSP, PRINCE2, PMI PMBOK, ISO 21502, ISO 31000, COSO ERM); programme governance and RAID practice

guidedInputs.label: Programme context
guidedInputs.description: Describe the regulatory-change programme: the driving instrument(s), the obliged entity, current phase, and the binding application/compliance dates you are working toward.
guidedInputs.placeholder: e.g. AMLR (EU) 2024/1624 + DORA (EU) 2022/2554 readiness programme for a Swedish e-money institution (~120 FTE). Phase 2 (Data & Systems), ~55% complete. AMLR application 10 July 2027; AMLA operational since July 2025 (direct supervision from Jan 2028); DORA already applicable since 17 Jan 2025 with a live ICT third-party register obligation.

guidedInputs.label: Regulatory instruments in scope
guidedInputs.description: Which instruments is this programme delivering against? Drives interpretation-risk and supervisory-deadline analysis.

options.label: AMLA Reg (EU) 2024/1620 — authority operational since Jul 2025, direct supervision from Jan 2028
MiCA (EU) 2023/1114 — ART/EMT from Jun 2024, CASP regime from Dec 2024
EU AI Act (EU) 2024/1689 — phased to Aug 2026/2027

guidedInputs.label: Entity jurisdiction(s) & supervisor
guidedInputs.description: Which jurisdiction(s) and national competent authority set the supervisory timetable and transposition rules for this programme?

guidedInputs.label: Risk dimensions to emphasise
guidedInputs.description: Which programme-risk categories should the taxonomy and register prioritise?

options.label: Supervisory-deadline risk (application dates, transposition, day-one obligations)
Resourcing & capacity risk (SME availability, vendor reliance, key-person)
Scope-creep risk (perimeter expansion, gold-plating, requirement drift)
Evidence / audit-trail risk (traceability, defensibility, examination readiness)
Data & technology delivery risk (migration, system change, data quality)
Governance & decision risk (mandate, accountability, escalation latency)
Change-adoption & operating-model risk (BAU handover, training, embedding)

guidedInputs.label: Programme governance maturity
guidedInputs.description: How established is the programme's governance and assurance today? Calibrates how aggressively to flag governance/escalation risk.

options.label: Forming — no formal SteerCo / RAID discipline yet
Established — SteerCo, RAID log, and stage gates in place
Assured — independent assurance / three-lines model operating

guidedInputs.label: Known issues, concerns, or prior findings
guidedInputs.description: Describe known risks, audit/assurance findings, missed milestones, contested interpretations, or vendor problems already on your radar.
guidedInputs.placeholder: e.g. AMLA RTS on CDD still in draft — our build assumes the consultation text. Vendor for the screening platform slipped 6 weeks. Internal audit flagged weak traceability between requirements and test evidence. UBO data-model decision contested between Compliance and Data teams.

exampleInput: We run a combined AMLR + DORA readiness programme for a Swedish e-money institution (~120 FTE, Finansinspektionen-supervised). We are in Phase 2 (Data & Systems), roughly 55% complete. AMLR (EU) 2024/1624 applies from 10 July 2027; AMLA (EU) 2024/1620 has been operational since July 2025 and begins direct supervision of selected entities from January 2028; DORA (EU) 2022/2554 has applied since 17 January 2025 and our ICT third-party register is a live day-one obligation we are still completing. Build me a programme risk taxonomy and a populated RAID register. I am most worried about three things: (1) several AMLA RTS/ITS are still in draft, so our requirements may shift under us; (2) the AMLR application date is fixed and immovable while two upstream dependencies (the new screening platform and the UBO data model) are slipping; and (3) internal audit has already flagged weak traceability between our requirements and our test evidence, which is an examination-readiness problem. Give me a governance and escalation structure to manage it.

exampleValues.programme_context: Combined AMLR (EU) 2024/1624 + DORA (EU) 2022/2554 readiness programme for a Swedish e-money institution (~120 FTE), supervised by Finansinspektionen. Phase 2 (Data & Systems), ~55% complete. AMLR application 10 July 2027; AMLA operational since July 2025 with direct supervision from January 2028; DORA applicable since 17 Jan 2025 with the ICT third-party register still being completed.
exampleValues.known_concerns: Several AMLA RTS/ITS still in draft, so requirements may shift. Screening-platform vendor slipped 6 weeks and the UBO data model is contested between Compliance and Data. Internal audit flagged weak traceability between requirements and test evidence — an examination-readiness concern. AMLR application date (10 Jul 2027) is fixed and cannot move.
